name: furniture-design
description: Furniture designs and the published knowledge they are judged against. Kinds: source and clause (a publication and its verbatim, located statements, with the quantities they state), material (properties derived from clauses), requirement (a demand resting on clauses, with its limits and test conditions), piece, part and load. Rules: every clause quotes its source; requirements and materials rest on clauses; a piece in a requirement's scope is held to it; a piece stands in its stability cases (furniture/tipping_cases); a part bends within its longtime sag limit (Wood Handbook Eq. 9-2 to 9-4 and its creep guidance, furniture/deflection, with no shear term for a panel whose modulus was measured on the panel); a part is strong enough (Eq. 9-13 against the near-minimum modulus of rupture over the Handbook's factor for 10-year duration of load and safety); a part bends the way its material's values were measured; a part that swells and shrinks with the air has room to (Eq. 13-3, the moisture content of its climate from Eq. 4-5, kind climate), and is judged only where that equation holds; a joint is cut with a tool its connector takes, at its setting, in parts thick and wide enough for it (kinds tool, connector, joint; a maker's products are data in a package of their own). The rules carry no number a source states: limits and properties are read from the knowledge base.

vocabulary.description: A publication the knowledge base quotes: payload title-like name, publisher, year, identifier, url, sha256 of what was fetched, licence (public-domain or copyrighted) and, when the licence allows, capture (the path of the text kept in the repo). Its children are the clauses quoted from it.

A located statement of its parent source: payload locator (chapter, table, page) and quote (verbatim); transcribed when the statement is an equation or a table row text extraction cannot read, read from the page and marked as transcription. A clause of a copyrighted source carries its locator and no quote: the words are the publisher's, and the copy they can be checked against is kept where it may be. Its params are the quantities it states, converted to SI, provenance published.

params.(any): a quantity the clause states, in SI, its original wording in note

vocabulary.description: A material a part is made of. Its params are its properties, each derived_from the clauses it was computed from; a part links to it with `uses` and reads them as its own. payload form (solid wood, plywood, ...), measured_along (the direction its bending values were measured in: grain, face grain, or unstated when the source does not say) and modulus (true: corrected for shear deflection, so a shear term is added; apparent: measured on the panel with its shear deflection in it).

params.modulus_of_elasticity: EL, MPa (for a panel, its bending modulus as tested on the panel)
params.modulus_of_rupture: MPa, the mean bending strength the source states
params.design_bending_stress: MPa, the bending stress a part may be designed to
params.initial_share_of_longtime: the share of a permitted longtime deflection the initial deflection may reach (creep)

links.per: the clauses its properties come from

vocabulary.description: A demand a design can be checked against: payload measure (what it limits, e.g. overturning, longtime_sag), scope {category} when it applies to a category of piece, and the test conditions in words; params its limits and test conditions, and min_<x> for a scope threshold on the piece's x (height, mass, or a param the piece carries). A design may author its own requirement (a target it sets itself), provenance design-target.

params.limit: the largest value the measure may take
params.min_<x>: the piece is in scope only when its x reaches this

vocabulary.description: A piece of furniture: its parts beneath it. Frame: x across, y from the front (smallest y) to the back, z up from the floor, mm. payload category (e.g. clothing-storage-unit) brings it into a requirement's scope.

params.storage_volume: mm3, what it holds, when a requirement's scope reads it

links.stability_case: the overturning requirements it is held to

vocabulary.description: A component to make. payload shape {op: box, size: [x, y, z]} with sizes in mm or naming the part's params, transform {translate} placing its minimum corner relative to the enclosing part or piece (geometry@'s convention); extends (mm it opens towards the front) for a drawer or pull-out shelf; hinged for a door (not modelled yet); span_along (grain, face grain) for a part that bends: the way its grain runs along its span; shear_modulus naming the material property that is G for it (shear_modulus_lr for a board whose vertical faces are edge-grained, the common flat-sawn board lying flat; shear_modulus_lt for flat-grained vertical faces). A part that bends names its span, depth and thickness params and its Table 9-1 case. A part that swells and shrinks with the air (a floating panel) links the climate it lives in and its movement equation, names in payload across_grain the param that is its width across the grain and in dimensional_change the material property that moves it (dimensional_change_tangential for a flat-sawn face, dimensional_change_radial for a quartersawn one), and states the clearance it has.

params.mass: kg, when it is not its volume times its material's density
params.thickness: mm, the beam's depth h, and a joined panel's thickness
params.clearance: mm the part may grow across the grain before it is stopped

links.bends_as: the Table 9-1 clause for its loading and supports
links.sag_limit: the longtime-sag requirements it is held to
links.moves_per: the clause of the movement equation it is judged by

vocabulary.description: A machine or jig that cuts or drills what a joint needs: payload maker and what it does. A design names the tools it is made with; a connector names the tools that can cut its seat.

links.per: the clauses that say what it does

vocabulary.description: A manufactured element that joins parts (a knock-down fitting, a biscuit, a dowel): payload maker and setting (the machine setting its seat is cut at, when it has one); params its limits — min_width (mm, the narrowest part it may join), min_thickness_<cut> (mm, per kind of cut: edge, surface, intermediate, mitre), pull_out_<material> and shear_<material> (N) — each derived from a clause.

links.needs: the tools that can cut its seat; any one of them will do
links.per: the clauses its limits come from

vocabulary.description: Where parts are joined. Links joins (the parts), uses (the connector it is made with, whose limits it reads as its own) and made_with (the tools that cut it); payload cut (edge, surface, intermediate or mitre: which of the connector's min_thickness_<cut> applies) and setting (the machine setting it is cut at); param count (connectors in it). A joined part states its width and thickness.

links.made_with: the tools it is cut with

vocabulary.description: The air a piece lives in: params temperature (°C) and rh_min and rh_max, the driest and dampest relative humidity it sees, as decimals; a design states it (design-target) or a home measures it. It links emc_per to the equation that turns it into the moisture content wood settles at (furniture/emc).
Something a part carries: param mass (kg), payload distribution (uniform or a point), provenance published when a clause states it, design-target when the design does.

rules.name: a-clause-quotes-its-source
rules.expr: some(s, nodes('source'), s == parent(self)) and len(payload(self, 'locator', '')) > 0 and (len(payload(self, 'quote', '')) > 0 or payload(parent(self), 'licence', '') == 'copyrighted')
rules.description: A clause sits under the source it comes from, says where in it, and quotes it, unless the source is copyrighted: then it carries the values and the locator, and the words stay with their publisher.

rules.name: a-connector-rests-on-clauses
rules.expr: len(linked(self, 'per')) > 0 and every(c, linked(self, 'per'), some(k, nodes('clause'), k == c))
rules.description: A connector links `per` to the clauses its limits come from.

rules.name: a-joined-part-is-thick-enough-for-the-cut
rules.description: Every part a joint joins is at least as thick as its connector allows for the kind of cut the joint is (the connector's min_thickness_<cut>, read through `uses`).

rules.name: a-joined-part-is-wide-enough
rules.description: Every part a joint joins is at least as wide as its connector allows.

rules.name: a-joint-is-cut-with-a-tool-its-connector-takes
rules.expr: len(linked(self, 'made_with')) > 0 and every(c, linked(self, 'uses'), some(t, linked(c, 'needs'), some(m, linked(self, 'made_with'), m == t)))
rules.description: A joint names the tools it is cut with, and one of them is a tool its connector's seat can be cut with.

rules.name: a-joint-is-cut-at-its-connectors-setting
rules.expr: every(c, linked(self, 'uses'), payload(c, 'setting', '') == '' or payload(self, 'setting', '') == payload(c, 'setting', ''))
rules.description: When a connector's seat is cut at a machine setting, the joint says it is cut at that setting.

rules.name: a-requirement-rests-on-clauses
rules.expr: len(linked(self, 'per')) > 0 and every(c, linked(self, 'per'), some(k, nodes('clause'), k == c))
rules.description: A requirement links `per` to the clauses it rests on, and each is a clause in the tree; a target a design sets itself still names the clause that makes it a sensible measure.

rules.name: a-material-rests-on-clauses
rules.expr: len(linked(self, 'per')) > 0 and every(c, linked(self, 'per'), some(k, nodes('clause'), k == c))
rules.description: A material links `per` to the clauses its properties come from.

rules.name: a-load-acts-on-a-part
rules.expr: len(linked(self, 'on')) > 0 and every(p, linked(self, 'on'), some(k, nodes('part'), k == p))
rules.description: A load names the part it acts on.

rules.name: a-piece-is-held-to-what-applies-to-it
rules.description: A piece in a requirement's scope (its category, and every min_<x> threshold reached) links to that requirement, so the check that requirement asks for is run.

rules.name: a-piece-stands-in-its-stability-cases
rules.description: Under every overturning requirement a piece links as stability_case, the static moment about its front edge keeps it standing. A prediction of the physical test the requirement describes, not a substitute for it.

rules.name: a-beam-sags-within-its-limit
rules.expr: every(r, linked(self, 'sag_limit'), solve('furniture/deflection', self) <= param(self, 'initial_share_of_longtime') * param(r, 'limit'))
rules.description: Wood Handbook Equation (9-2) with (9-3) and (9-4), through furniture/deflection: the initial deflection of a part under its own weight and the loads on it is at most the share of each sag_limit's longtime limit that creep leaves (Chapter 9, Creep Deflections).

rules.name: a-beam-is-strong-enough
rules.expr: every(c, linked(self, 'bends_as'), param(c, 'km') * 9.80665 * (solve('furniture/mass', self) + sum(params_of(backlinked(self, 'on'), 'mass'))) * param(self, 'span') * 6 / (param(self, 'depth') * param(self, 'thickness') * param(self, 'thickness')) <= param(self, 'design_bending_stress'))
rules.description: Wood Handbook Equation (9-13): the largest bending stress M/S in a part, M = km W L for its Table 9-1 case and S = b h^2/6, under its own weight and the loads on it, is at most its material's design bending stress (the near-minimum modulus of rupture over the factor for duration of load and safety). W in N, lengths in mm, stresses in MPa.

rules.name: a-part-bends-the-way-its-material-was-tested
rules.expr: every(c, linked(self, 'bends_as'), every(m, linked(self, 'uses'), payload(self, 'span_along', '') == payload(m, 'measured_along', 'unstated')))
rules.description: A part that bends spans the way its material's bending values were measured (along the grain for solid wood, face grain along the span for plywood). A material whose source does not say which way it was bent (measured_along: unstated) judges no part's bending.

rules.name: a-moving-part-stays-where-its-equation-holds
rules.expr: every(c, linked(self, 'moves_in'), len(linked(self, 'moves_per')) == 1 and solve('furniture/emc', c, 'min') >= sum(params_of(linked(self, 'moves_per'), 'mc_min')) and solve('furniture/emc', c, 'max') <= sum(params_of(linked(self, 'moves_per'), 'mc_max')))
rules.description: The movement equation a part is judged by holds over a range of moisture content (Wood Handbook Eq. 13-3: 6% to 14%); in a climate that takes the wood outside it, the movement it predicts is not to be trusted, and this says so instead of answering.

rules.name: a-moving-part-has-room-to-move
rules.expr: every(c, linked(self, 'moves_in'), param(self, payload(self, 'across_grain')) * param(self, payload(self, 'dimensional_change')) * (solve('furniture/emc', c, 'max') - solve('furniture/emc', c, 'min')) <= param(self, 'clearance'))
rules.description: Wood Handbook Eq. 13-3: across the grain a part changes by its width times its material's dimensional change coefficient times the change in moisture content between the driest and dampest air of its climate (Eq. 4-5); its clearance takes at least that.

solvers.name: furniture/deflection
solvers.description:
mm: the initial deflection of `part` under its own weight and every load `on` it,
Wood Handbook Equation (9-2) with (9-3) and (9-4): kb W L³/(E I) + ks W L/(G A′), I =
b h³/12, A′ = 5 b h/6, kb and ks from the one Table 9-1 clause the part links as
`bends_as`, L, b, h its `span`, `depth` and `thickness`, E its material's
`modulus_of_elasticity`. The shear term's G is the material property the part names in
payload `shear_modulus`. A material whose payload says its modulus is `apparent` (a
panel's bending modulus, measured on the panel with its shear deflection in it) takes no
shear term: adding one would count that deflection twice.

solvers.name: furniture/emc
solvers.description:
%: the moisture content wood settles at in `climate` at its `end` ('min' or 'max'):
the climate's `temperature` (°C) and `rh_<end>` (relative humidity, a decimal), through
the equation of the clause it links as `emc_per`, whose params are W, K, K1 and K2 as
polynomials in T (`W_0`, `W_1`, `W_2`, ...). Wood Handbook Equation (4-5).

solvers.name: furniture/height
solvers.description: mm: from the floor to the top of the highest part.

solvers.name: furniture/overturning_margin
solvers.description:
N·mm: the moment holding the piece down about its front tipping edge, minus the one
tipping it, under the test conditions the requirement `case` states — its params
`tilt_block` (mm, the rear supports raised so the piece leans forward), `point_mass`
(kg on the front top edge of an open extendible element, each in turn, the worst one
kept), and `fill_density` with `fill_share` (kg/m3 of storage volume in every
extendible element, when they hold at least that share of the piece's
`storage_volume`). Every extendible element is open. Positive: it stays standing.

solvers.name: furniture/tipping_cases
solvers.description:
How many of the requirements `piece` links as `stability_case` it is predicted to
tip under.

solvers.name: furniture/unheld
solvers.description: How many requirements apply to `piece` (in_scope) that it does not link to.

children.name: Safety Standard for Clothing Storage Units, direct final rule, 88 FR 28403 (16 CFR part 1261)

payload.publisher: U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission, Federal Register
payload.note: The rule adopts ASTM F2057-23 by reference; its test methods are ASTM's and copyrighted. What is quoted here is the Commission's public description of them.

payload.quote: Clothing storage unit means any free-standing furniture item manufactured in the United States or imported for use in the United States that is intended for the storage of clothing, typical of bedroom furniture.
Each clothing storage unit that is subject to ASTM F2057-23, Standard Safety Specification for Clothing Storage Units, approved on February 1, 2023, shall comply with ASTM F2057-23.
Testing of all clothing storage units as specified by the Commission, including those 27 inches and above in height
The ASTM standard excludes units weighing less than 30 pounds empty.

Staff therefore concluded that the Commission could find that, based on tip-over data, testing units having a storage volume less than 3.2 cubic feet is not ``reasonably necessary'' to protect children from injury or death.

payload.locator: Preamble II.B, describing ASTM F2057-23 section 9.2.1, 88 FR 28405
payload.quote: Section 9.2.1 of the ASTM standard, Simulated Clothing Load, is a test conducted on a hard, level, and flat test surface with extendible elements and doors open and, if 50 percent or more of the storage volume is extended, the unit is to be filled with a ``simulated clothing load.'' The fill weight in extendible elements is calculated using a density of 8.5 pounds per cubic foot of volume
All extendible elements are opened and must remain open for 30 seconds without tip over.

payload.quote: Clothing storage unit means any free-standing furniture item manufactured in the United States or imported for use in the United States that is intended for the storage of clothing, typical of bedroom furniture.

Testing of all clothing storage units as specified by the Commission, including those 27 inches and above in height
